title: Algorithmic Trading: Causal Research and Guarded Paper Systems

stageOutcomes.outcome: Build a typed, timestamp-aware data fixture and reconcile a simple delayed-signal paper ledger.
stageOutcomes.evidence: A runnable local baseline with data-quality failures, availability-time checks and hand-calculated golden cases.

stageOutcomes.outcome: Implement a causal simulator and report chronological out-of-sample results after costs.
stageOutcomes.evidence: A tested event loop, conservative fills, trial registry and frozen walk-forward report.

stageOutcomes.outcome: Evaluate constrained portfolios and model-based signals under dependence, leakage and adverse regimes.
stageOutcomes.evidence: A portfolio/risk report and an adversarial validation pack that catches contaminated experiments.

stageOutcomes.outcome: Release a reproducible, disconnected paper engine with monitoring, durable halts and recovery controls.
stageOutcomes.evidence: A replayable capstone bundle, no-network execution boundary, kill-switch/restart drill and independent audit memo.

resources.title: pandas: Time series / date functionality
resources.notes: Public HTML covers timestamps, resampling and time zones. Pin the version used in your experiment; a business-day frequency is not an exchange holiday calendar. pandas is free and can run locally.

resources.title: pandas.merge_asof reference
resources.notes: Verified sorted-key requirement and backward/forward/nearest, tolerance and allow_exact_matches parameters. The function does not automatically identify a correct availability timestamp or eliminate financial leakage.

resources.title: scikit-learn: TimeSeriesSplit
resources.notes: Public reference documents expanding training sets, gap and test_size, with an equal-spacing caveat for comparable fold durations. It does not automatically purge overlapping financial labels or fit transformations without leakage.

resources.title: QuantConnect documentation: Research Guide
resources.notes: Read hypothesis development and research pitfalls only. This curriculum requires neither the hosted platform, market-data subscription, brokerage account nor paid features. Implement original synthetic exercises locally.

resources.title: QuantConnect documentation: Reality Modeling key concepts
resources.notes: Public descriptions of fills, fees, slippage, portfolio and capacity models. Defaults assume liquid assets; realistic live performance is not guaranteed. Use this as a taxonomy, not a requirement to use the service.

resources.title: Python: unittest framework reference
resources.license: Official Python documentation; link-only in this curriculum
resources.notes: Use Basic example, test discovery and assert methods for local deterministic cases. No external service or account is needed; standard-library tests are sufficient for the core route.

modules.title: 01. Programming and point-in-time research data
modules.description: Start with inspectable local files, explicit types and data that were actually available at each decision.

lessons.title: Create a small, reproducible Python research contract
objectives: Separate pure calculations from file and clock access.
Validate a synthetic price record and fail visibly on invalid input.

topics.title: Program boundaries
details: Inputs, outputs, units and error conditions belong in the contract.
A research function must not place orders or depend on an uncontrolled current time.

topics.title: Local reproducibility
details: Pin interpreter and dependency versions and record the command.
Keep fixture generation deterministic and original source data immutable.

video.locator: CS50P Week 0 - Functions: parameters, return values and decomposition; reuse the Common Foundation lecture.

reading.locator: Python Tutorial sections 4.8 Defining Functions and 8 Errors and Exceptions; define contracts and explicit invalid-record errors.

assignment.title: A no-network price transformation
instructions: Write a pure function accepting symbol, timestamp, price and quantity with explicit units.
Use six invented records: valid, missing price, negative quantity, duplicate ID, invalid timestamp and non-finite price.
Return valid normalized records and an explicit rejection report; document a local command and environment without any broker library.
deliverables: Small Python module and six test cases
acceptanceCriteria: No invalid or non-finite number reaches return calculations.
Errors identify the rejected record and reason rather than replacing values with zero.
Repeated runs of the same fixture are identical and require no network.

questions.prompt: A missing price should become which of these?
choices: An explicit invalid-record outcome
Zero without a warning
The next future price
questions.answer: An explicit invalid-record outcome
questions.explanation: Silent zero substitution corrupts returns; a future fill can introduce leakage. Rejection or a declared missing-data policy must be visible.

questions.prompt: Why inject a decision timestamp instead of reading the current clock inside a research function?
questions.answer: An explicit timestamp makes availability checks reproducible and prevents results from depending on when the function happens to run.
questions.explanation: Time is part of the model input, not an invisible dependency.

reviewPrompts: Can the function be tested without a file, clock or network?

lessons.title: Normalize bars without inventing market observations
objectives: Handle time zones, duplicates and session boundaries.
Distinguish a missing observation from a zero-volume or closed-market interval.

topics.title: Temporal contracts
details: State whether a timestamp names bar opening, closing or publication.
A local date, UTC instant and exchange session are not interchangeable.

topics.title: Quality policy
details: Missing bars and duplicate revisions require different handling.
Forward filling for a mark is not permission to invent tradable volume.

reading.locator: Time zone handling; Resampling; DateOffset objects. Explain why generic business-day offsets alone do not encode an exchange's calendar.

assignment.title: A bar-quality quarantine
instructions: Create a 12-row synthetic bar file with one duplicate, one out-of-order row, one missing interval and one ambiguous naive timestamp.
Normalize only records with an explicit time-zone policy; produce a quarantine report for unresolved rows.
Resample a valid subset and record closed/open interval choices, with a test showing that resampling cannot create execution volume.
acceptanceCriteria: No local-time ambiguity is silently guessed.
Duplicate resolution preserves provenance and is deterministic.
A missing interval cannot create a simulated trade by forward filling volume.

questions.prompt: What does a missing one-minute bar prove?
choices: That the price was zero
That unlimited volume traded at the last price
Only that the observation is missing under the feed contract
questions.answer: Only that the observation is missing under the feed contract
questions.explanation: A missing record may reflect closure, no trades or feed failure. Its meaning must be established before resampling or filling.

questions.prompt: Why must a bar-close signal not use a bar labelled by its opening time without further checks?
questions.answer: The completed bar may contain future observations relative to the label; its close becomes available only after the bar ends and is published.
questions.explanation: Labels and availability are different clocks.

reviewPrompts: What is the earliest instant at which this bar is usable?

lessons.title: Build an availability-time and universe-history join
objectives: Join features by publication time rather than their economic period.
Preserve revisions, delistings and historical membership.

topics.title: Point-in-time data
details: Event time describes what happened; availability time describes when it could be known.
Revised values must not replace earlier vintages in an old decision.

topics.title: Survivorship and actions
details: Today's surviving instruments are not yesterday's full universe.
Raw prices and adjusted series need explicit corporate-action and publication conventions.

reading.locator: Parameters direction, tolerance, allow_exact_matches and by; use sorted availability times and backward matches, with an explicit publication-latency rule.

assignment.title: A two-clock counterexample fixture
instructions: Invent an earnings record for period-end day 1 released on day 5 and revised on day 9.
Evaluate decisions on days 3, 6 and 10 using only then-available vintages; include one instrument removed from the universe on day 8.
Compare an intentionally wrong event-date join with the correct availability join and retain a failing regression test.
deliverables: Join tests with expected values at three decision dates
acceptanceCriteria: Day 3 cannot see the release and day 6 cannot see the revision.
The removed instrument is retained in earlier membership and loss history.
Tolerance, equality and adjustment policies are documented rather than delegated blindly to merge_asof.

questions.prompt: A day-1 value is first published on day 5. Which decision can legitimately use it?
choices: A day-6 decision, subject to delivery latency
A day-2 decision because the period ended
Every past decision after later revision
questions.answer: A day-6 decision, subject to delivery latency
questions.explanation: Economic period labels do not make a value observable. Publication and actual availability must precede the decision.

questions.prompt: How can removing delisted instruments bias a backtest?
questions.answer: It can remove failed or adverse histories that an earlier investor could have held, overstating the apparent performance of the selected universe.
questions.explanation: Historical membership is part of the data-generating process, not just a current lookup table.

reviewPrompts: Which future fact could still enter through metadata?

modules.title: 02. Returns, baselines and accounting invariants
modules.description: Establish a correct simple system before optimizing or adding machine learning.

lessons.title: Compute returns from a cash-and-position ledger
objectives: Reconcile equity, cash, holdings, dividends and fees.
Distinguish simple returns, compounding and valuation assumptions.

topics.title: Accounting first
details: Equity is cash plus marked holdings under a declared mark policy.
Splits and dividends must not be double counted in prices and cash.

topics.title: Return measurement
details: Compound period returns rather than adding percentages.
External deposits are not trading profits.

reading.locator: Chapter 11 Corporate actions and impact on stock prices; distinguish mechanical price adjustments from cash entitlements.

assignment.title: A hand-checkable portfolio ledger
instructions: Start with cash 1000, buy five units at 100 with total fee 2, then mark at 110 and credit a synthetic dividend of 1 per unit.
Add a two-for-one split, preserving equity under a corresponding halved mark.
Test a deposit as an external flow, not strategy P&L, and declare whether dividend-adjusted prices are excluded.
acceptanceCriteria: Equity before the split is 1053 under the specified events.
The split preserves equity and doubles units.
Dividends and external deposits cannot be double counted as return.

questions.prompt: Returns of +10% followed by -10% leave what total percentage return?
questions.explanation: 1.10 times 0.90 equals 0.99, so the total return is -1%, not zero.

questions.prompt: Why does adding cash to an account not prove strategy profitability?
questions.answer: A deposit is an external flow; performance must separate it from gains or losses earned on exposure.
questions.explanation: A growing equity balance can reflect new funding rather than trading return.

reviewPrompts: Can every change in equity be explained by an event or mark?

lessons.title: Implement a delayed signal and simple baselines
objectives: Separate observation, decision and simulated execution timestamps.
Compare a candidate rule with flat and constant-exposure baselines.

topics.title: Signal timing
details: A closing observation cannot justify an earlier same-bar fill.
A rolling window's alignment must be explicit.

topics.title: Baseline design
details: A simple baseline can expose accidental look-ahead or exposure differences.
All comparators need the same data and accounting conventions.

reading.locator: Hypothesis Development: state a cause/effect claim before implementing a rule. Use original synthetic rules, not the page's suggested trading examples.

assignment.title: A one-step-delayed toy signal
instructions: Use twelve invented closes and a three-observation trailing average; begin decisions only after a full window exists.
Execute any position change at the next available synthetic observation, with no intrabar price assumptions.
Run flat, constant-one-unit and delayed-signal comparators through the same ledger and print the timestamp of every decision/fill.
deliverables: A timing diagram and alignment test
acceptanceCriteria: Changing a future price cannot change an earlier signal.
Warm-up observations produce no unsupported trades.
Baselines use identical cost and mark policies.

questions.prompt: A signal calculated from today's close can safely use which declared paper execution assumption?
choices: Yesterday's close
The next available observation after the decision
Today's low selected after seeing the full bar
questions.answer: The next available observation after the decision
questions.explanation: The decision cannot cause a trade before its inputs become available. Even next-observation execution remains a disclosed approximation.

questions.prompt: What does a future-perturbation test check?
questions.answer: It changes later data and verifies that earlier features and decisions remain unchanged.
questions.explanation: This directly probes causal dependence and can reveal centered windows or improperly fitted transformations.

reviewPrompts: What exactly is known when the signal is emitted?

lessons.title: Prove the baseline with golden traces and invariants
objectives: Use hand-derived cases before trusting aggregate metrics.
Test conservation, determinism and explicit failure behavior.

topics.title: Golden examples
details: Small expected event traces reveal timing and sign errors.
A passing profit metric can hide compensating accounting mistakes.

topics.title: Invariants
details: Filled plus remaining quantity must match accepted quantity.
Duplicate events must not create duplicate cash effects.

video.locator: CS50P Week 5 - Unit Tests: test boundaries and failing cases; apply to the original ledger rather than copying course problems.

reading.locator: Basic example, test discovery, assertEqual and assertRaises. Write golden-state assertions and explicit rejection tests.

assignment.title: Beginner evidence gate: a trusted local baseline
instructions: Write golden traces for no trades, one round trip, split/dividend, duplicate event and missing price.
Add invariants for cash/position reconciliation and decision-before-fill timing.
Publish one command that runs fixture validation, baseline replay and tests in a clean local environment.
deliverables: Five golden ledgers and a reproducibility README in the learner's project
acceptanceCriteria: At least one intentionally broken timing or fee implementation fails a targeted test.
Duplicate events are rejected or idempotently ignored with an explicit report.
Results reconcile exactly on integer-unit fixtures; any floating tolerance is justified.

questions.prompt: Which assertion most directly catches charging a fee twice?
choices: Expected cash after a one-trade golden case
The final chart has a title
The strategy has many trades
questions.answer: Expected cash after a one-trade golden case
questions.explanation: A hand-derived cash balance isolates the fee effect. Presentation and trade counts do not establish accounting correctness.

questions.prompt: Why retain the test that first exposed a bug?
questions.answer: It records the failure contract and prevents future changes from silently reintroducing the same error.
questions.explanation: A regression suite is evidence of known failure handling, not proof that every possible bug is absent.

reviewPrompts: Which invariant fails earliest when an event is duplicated?

modules.title: 03. Event-driven backtesting and realistic frictions
modules.description: Make event order, fills, capacity and transaction costs inspectable.

lessons.title: Build a causal event loop and explicit order state
objectives: Order data, signal, risk, order and fill events deterministically.
Separate a requested action from a confirmed simulated effect.

topics.title: Event ordering
details: Tied timestamps need a documented stable tie-breaker.
Publication, processing and fill latency are separate assumptions.

topics.title: State transitions
details: Pending, accepted, partially filled, cancelled and expired states have permitted transitions.
Rejected orders cannot affect inventory.

reading.locator: Introduction and reality-model categories: distinguish fill, fee and portfolio responsibilities rather than hiding them in the signal function.

assignment.title: A deterministic paper event engine
instructions: Implement typed events for data arrival, decision, risk approval, order and fill using an in-memory queue.
Define tie-breakers for same-time events and reject a fill that precedes the approved order.
Replay a cancellation/partial-fill race and compare a golden final state.
acceptanceCriteria: Every fill references an accepted order and a causally later available observation.
Identical event streams yield identical transitions.
Invalid transitions surface an error without mutating cash or positions.

questions.prompt: What is required when two events share a timestamp?
choices: A documented deterministic ordering rule
Whichever order produces more profit
Random ordering without a recorded seed
questions.answer: A documented deterministic ordering rule
questions.explanation: Same-time processing can change available information or position state. The rule must be stable and justified, not outcome-selected.

questions.prompt: Why not update positions when an order is merely submitted?
questions.answer: Submission is intent; rejection, delay or partial execution can change the actual effect. Positions should reflect confirmed simulated fills.
questions.explanation: Conflating intent and execution makes risk and cash accounting unreliable.

reviewPrompts: Which transition proves that inventory actually changed?

lessons.title: Model spread, fees, impact and capacity limits
objectives: Specify disjoint transaction-cost components.
Stress execution as order size becomes large relative to available volume.

topics.title: Friction model
details: Price-side slippage and separate fees must not overlap.
Turnover drives repeated costs even for low net exposure.

topics.title: Capacity
details: A participation limit bounds assumed available volume.
Historical volume is not a guarantee of executable liquidity.

reading.locator: Reality models for fees, fills, slippage and capacity; note the documentation's highly-liquid-assets default assumption.

assignment.title: A size-sensitive cost model
instructions: Define an invented half-spread, per-order fee and increasing size/volume impact term with stated units.
Cap simulated fills at 10% of an invented bar's 200-unit volume and carry or expire the remainder according to policy.
Compare net results at 1x and 2x costs without fitting the assumptions to the preferred strategy.
acceptanceCriteria: At most 20 units fill under the stated participation assumption.
Buy and sell adverse slippage have correct opposite price signs.
Zero-volume bars produce no market fill and an explicit reason.

questions.prompt: A paper participation cap is 10% of 200 units. How many units may fill?
questions.explanation: 0.10 times 200 is 20. This is a modelling limit, not a promise that even those 20 units are available in a real queue.

questions.prompt: Why should adverse sell slippage lower the fill price?
questions.answer: A worse sell receives less money, whereas a worse buy pays more; applying the same signed price offset to both sides can overstate performance.
questions.explanation: Cost sign conventions must follow the cash-flow direction.

reviewPrompts: Which assumption breaks first as capital scales up?

lessons.title: Handle partial fills, missing data and cancellation races
objectives: Preserve a quantity-conserving lifecycle under adverse events.
Mark unsupported execution assumptions visibly rather than fabricating liquidity.

topics.title: Failure cases
details: Rejected and expired orders retain IDs and reasons.
A cancel request may be overtaken by an earlier fill.

topics.title: Bar ambiguity
details: OHLC data cannot establish stop/limit ordering.
Missing feed data should trigger an explicit halt or no-fill state.

reading.locator: Chapter 9 The Trading Terminal: distinguish order instructions from executions; Chapter 15 market depth: available quantity is finite.

assignment.title: A fill-state adversarial suite
instructions: Send a 30-unit paper order, fill 12, then interleave a 5-unit fill with a cancellation acknowledgement.
Add duplicate acknowledgement, expiry, absent next bar and a bar touching both stop and limit.
Specify the conservative outcome of each ambiguity and reconcile all remaining quantities.
acceptanceCriteria: The 17 confirmed filled units remain held after cancellation.
Filled plus cancelled/remaining quantity never exceeds the accepted quantity.
An unsupported profitable intrabar ordering is not silently assumed.

questions.prompt: A 30-unit order fills 12 then 5 before the remainder is cancelled. How many units were filled?
questions.explanation: Cancellation affects only the remaining 13 units; it does not undo the 17 already filled.

questions.prompt: What evidence should accompany an ambiguous-bar policy?
questions.answer: The policy version, the affected events and sensitivity to a conservative alternative should be recorded.
questions.explanation: Making uncertainty inspectable is more honest than treating an arbitrary assumption as observed execution.

reviewPrompts: Does every exceptional path preserve inventory and audit history?

modules.title: 04. Walk-forward evaluation and research selection
modules.description: Keep chronology, preprocessing, parameter selection and final evidence separate.

lessons.title: Design walk-forward folds and protect label horizons
objectives: Implement chronological training, validation and final test blocks.
Purge overlapping labels and fit preprocessing only within each training fold.

topics.title: Split design
details: Expanding and rolling windows answer different stability questions.
A gap measured in rows is not automatically a purge based on label end-times.

topics.title: Leakage beyond rows
details: Scaling, imputation and feature selection can leak if fitted globally.
Uneven time spacing requires care when comparing fold durations.

video.locator: 5.Py Cross-Validation I 2023: contrast ordinary cross-validation with the chronological, overlap-aware design required here.

reading.locator: TimeSeriesSplit definition, equal-spacing caveat, gap and test_size examples. Add explicit label-interval purging; the library does not infer it.

assignment.title: An interval-aware walk-forward splitter
instructions: Create 60 equally spaced synthetic observations with labels using the next three observations.
Build three chronological folds and a separate untouched final block; exclude any training label whose horizon crosses into validation.
Fit a scaler only on each training portion and test that changing validation values does not change its parameters.
acceptanceCriteria: No training label overlaps a validation interval.
Final-test values cannot affect parameter or feature selection.
Fold duration, training size and gap/purge policy are documented.

questions.prompt: TimeSeriesSplit alone automatically fixes which issue?
choices: It orders the row-based train/test splits
It purges every overlapping label
It prevents a scaler fitted on all data
questions.answer: It orders the row-based train/test splits
questions.explanation: The caller must still handle availability, overlap, preprocessing and selection. Chronology is necessary but not sufficient.

questions.prompt: When must a training observation be purged for a three-period forward label?
questions.answer: When any part of the label's outcome interval reaches the validation or test interval under the declared boundary policy.
questions.explanation: The training row's timestamp can precede validation while its label still contains validation-period information.

reviewPrompts: What information can enter through labels rather than features?

lessons.title: Control trial selection and overfitting claims
objectives: Record all candidate experiments and selection decisions.
Explain why multiple tries weaken a winner's apparent evidence.

topics.title: Research registry
details: Each change to data, rules or costs is a distinct version.
Failed and abandoned trials remain part of the search history.

topics.title: Multiplicity
details: The best observed score is selected and therefore optimistic.
A final block cannot serve repeatedly as a model-development oracle.

video.locator: 13.Py Multiple Testing I 2023: use the selection problem as a warning, not as permission to treat dependent trading trials as independent tests.

reading.locator: Hypothesis Development and the warning against developing a hypothesis from test results. Record every deviation as a new trial.

assignment.title: A transparent six-trial registry
instructions: Try six predeclared variants on development data generated with no known predictive signal.
Record configuration, data version, selection metric, cost assumption and result for every trial, including errors.
Select using development folds, freeze the winner and explain the limitations before opening the final block.
deliverables: Selection memo and final-test access log
acceptanceCriteria: All six trials and their failures are retained.
Selection never consults the final block.
The memo does not equate the best in-sample score with an established edge.

questions.prompt: What happens to evidential strength when only the best of many trials is reported?
choices: Independent confirmation is created
Selection bias is hidden
Trading costs disappear
questions.answer: Selection bias is hidden
questions.explanation: Searching many variants can find a lucky high score. Omitting the search history conceals how the result was selected.

questions.prompt: What should happen when the final block inspires a new feature?
questions.answer: Treat the block as development information for that new version and seek genuinely new evaluation evidence rather than reusing it as untouched proof.
questions.explanation: The information boundary follows actual decisions, not labels in a report.

reviewPrompts: Could a reader reconstruct how many opportunities you had to get lucky?

lessons.title: Report net performance, uncertainty and failure honestly
objectives: Combine return, exposure, turnover, drawdown and benchmark information.
Qualify ratios and confidence estimates under serial dependence.

topics.title: Metric contracts
details: State frequency, annualization and treatment of idle periods.
A high ratio on a short sample can be unstable or undefined.

topics.title: Evaluation narrative
details: Report worst folds and cost sensitivity, not only an average.
A negative result can be a successful research outcome.

reading.locator: Sections 5.8 Evaluating point forecast accuracy and 5.10 Time series cross-validation: distinguish fit error, evaluation error and rolling-origin evidence.

assignment.title: Intermediate evidence gate: the cost-aware OOS report
instructions: Run the frozen candidate, flat baseline and simple constant exposure on untouched synthetic data.
Report net/gross P&L, maximum drawdown, turnover, exposure, trade count, per-fold outcomes and doubled-cost sensitivity.
Include an undefined-ratio case, sample/dependence caveats and the full registry/ledger links.
acceptanceCriteria: The report ties to the accounting ledger and discloses all cost assumptions.
Zero variance or no trades does not yield a fabricated infinite success score.
No annualized statistic or small synthetic sample is presented as a profitability forecast.

questions.prompt: A risk-adjusted ratio has a zero denominator. What should the report do?
choices: Mark it undefined and explain the case
Replace it with a very large positive number
Drop the period without disclosure
questions.answer: Mark it undefined and explain the case
questions.explanation: Undefined metrics are data, not an opportunity to improve the presentation. The underlying return and exposure should remain visible.

questions.prompt: Why can naive square-root-of-time annualization mislead?
questions.answer: It relies on assumptions about sampling, dependence and variance stability that may not hold for clustered or serially correlated strategy returns.
questions.explanation: Declare the convention and its limitations instead of implying additional observations or certainty.

reviewPrompts: What part of the report would change if costs doubled?

modules.title: 05. Portfolio construction and risk enforcement
modules.description: Constrain positions, cash and correlated risk before admitting paper orders.

lessons.title: Implement pretrade sizing and aggregate exposure checks
objectives: Convert a risk target into feasible rounded quantities.
Enforce cash, gross exposure and loss limits in one explicit admission decision.

topics.title: Sizing constraints
details: Volatility estimates and stop distances are uncertain inputs.
Rounding and minimum quantities can make a target infeasible.

topics.title: Risk state
details: Pending orders consume capacity until resolved.
Rejection reasons must be observable and reproducible.

reading.locator: Chapters 11-13 Position Sizing for active traders; evaluate the assumptions and apply additional aggregate/pending-order constraints.

assignment.title: A pure paper-risk admission function
instructions: Use invented capital 10000, per-order notional cap 2000 and gross cap 4000; include pending orders in exposure.
Evaluate a batch with rounded sizes, insufficient cash, duplicate intent and an already-breached daily loss limit.
Return an accept/reject record with the evaluated inputs and rule version.
acceptanceCriteria: Pending orders cannot bypass the gross cap.
Zero or non-finite risk estimates cannot create an unbounded size.
A breached daily limit rejects all new exposure until explicit clearance.

questions.prompt: Existing gross exposure is 2500 and pending exposure is 1000 against a 4000 cap. What remaining notional capacity is available?
questions.explanation: 4000 minus 2500 minus 1000 is 500. Ignoring pending orders would overstate capacity.

questions.prompt: Why reject a zero volatility estimate rather than divide the risk target by it?
questions.answer: It may reflect a short, stale or constant data sample, and division would create undefined or unbounded exposure.
questions.explanation: An invalid risk estimate is a reason to stop and inspect inputs, not a free allocation.

reviewPrompts: What commitments are not yet visible in holdings but still consume risk?

lessons.title: Construct a constrained multi-asset paper portfolio
objectives: Compare transparent equal-weight and risk-aware allocations.
Stress estimation sensitivity, turnover and concentration constraints.

topics.title: Portfolio inputs
details: Covariance estimates are noisy and can be unstable.
Weights are targets; quantity, cash and cost constraints govern execution.

topics.title: Allocation trade-offs
details: A lower estimated variance need not imply lower future tail loss.
Rebalancing can improve target adherence while raising costs.

reading.locator: Chapters 3-5 Variance, Covariance and Portfolio Variance; Chapters 8-9 Portfolio Optimization. Challenge input stability rather than maximizing a backtest score.

assignment.title: A three-asset allocation challenge
instructions: Generate three synthetic return streams with a recorded seed and an explicit shared-factor structure.
Compare equal weights with a capped inverse-volatility allocation, including transaction costs and rounding.
Perturb the estimation window and correlations; record concentration, turnover and feasibility, including any inability to meet targets.
acceptanceCriteria: Weights and residual cash reconcile after rounding.
No asset exceeds the declared cap, including a rejected infeasible case.
Evaluation is on later observations, not the estimation window.

questions.prompt: What is a key weakness of an allocation optimized on estimated covariance?
choices: It must use identical weights in every future period
Sensitivity to estimation error and changing relationships
It cannot express concentration constraints mathematically
questions.answer: Sensitivity to estimation error and changing relationships
questions.explanation: The matrix is an estimate from a limited regime. Constraints and stress tests help expose, but cannot remove, that uncertainty.

questions.prompt: Why report turnover alongside target weights?
questions.answer: Reaching targets requires trades, which consume liquidity and incur costs; frequent weight changes can overwhelm an apparent allocation benefit.
questions.explanation: A portfolio is an executable sequence of transitions, not just a static vector.

reviewPrompts: Does the allocation survive a small change in its estimates?

lessons.title: Combine gap, leverage and funding stress
objectives: Distinguish accounting solvency from available cash.
Test correlated shocks and delayed liquidation against operational limits.

topics.title: Tail scenarios
details: Gap and liquidity shocks can invalidate normal-period estimates.
Collateral is not maximum loss.

topics.title: Funding
details: Cash calls may arrive before offsetting gains settle.
A halt stops new risk but does not erase existing obligations.

video.locator: Forward and Futures Contracts: mark-to-market and obligations. Use only invented contracts in the local simulator.

reading.locator: Chapters 4 Leverage & Payoff and 5 Margin & M2M; separate price exposure from collateral and timing of cash calls.

assignment.title: A stressed cash-availability simulator
instructions: Add a synthetic margined contract and a separate unsettled positive cash flow to the paper ledger.
Apply a joint price gap, higher margin requirement and one-session exit delay.
Record when cash is insufficient and prevent the engine from treating an unrealized offset as immediately spendable.
deliverables: Stress event stream and liquidity ladder
acceptanceCriteria: Collateral, notional, realized cash and unsettled flows are distinct fields.
A positive marked equity value can coexist with an explicitly detected cash shortfall.
Halted state does not delete existing positions or obligations.

questions.prompt: Can a portfolio with positive marked equity face a funding failure?
choices: No, any positive mark is immediately spendable
Yes, cash may be unavailable when obligations fall due
No, margin caps all losses
questions.answer: Yes, cash may be unavailable when obligations fall due
questions.explanation: Settlement timing, collateral and realizability matter. Balance-sheet value is not the same as ready cash.

questions.prompt: What remains after a no-new-orders kill switch activates?
questions.answer: Existing positions, pending effects and funding or settlement obligations still require reconciliation and a controlled response.
questions.explanation: A stop control prevents additional risk; it is not a magical liquidation or rollback of the economic state.

reviewPrompts: Which obligation arrives before its supposed hedge pays?

modules.title: 06. Robust signals, model evaluation and leakage audits
modules.description: Add complexity only when evidence survives simple baselines and independent challenges.

lessons.title: Challenge stationarity and parameter stability
objectives: Recognize shifting mean, volatility and dependence.
Use stability analysis without choosing parameters on future regimes.

topics.title: Time-series behavior
details: A price level and its changes have different statistical properties.
Apparent mean reversion can disappear after a structural change.

topics.title: Robustness checks
details: Inspect rolling diagnostics and performance by regime.
A broad stable parameter region is more credible than a sharp optimum, but proves no future edge.

video.locator: Lecture 8: regression and stationarity. Translate the assumptions into explicit diagnostics on an invented series.

reading.locator: Section 9.1 Stationarity and differencing; distinguish a modelling assumption from proof that a financial signal will persist.

assignment.title: A structural-break counterexample
instructions: Generate a series with a known mean or volatility change at a recorded boundary, retaining the generating assumptions.
Compare rolling diagnostics and a frozen strategy across before/after windows without retuning on the second window.
Report parameter sensitivity and one condition that should pause research rather than trigger automatic optimization.
acceptanceCriteria: The regime boundary and generation process are disclosed.
The second regime is not used to claim an untouched optimized result.
The report distinguishes lack of detected change from evidence of stationarity.

questions.prompt: Not rejecting a stationarity-related test on a short sample proves what?
choices: That the test has high power against every plausible regime shift
Very little beyond the test's result under its assumptions
That chronological folds can now be replaced by shuffled folds
questions.answer: Very little beyond the test's result under its assumptions
questions.explanation: Low power, model assumptions and regime changes limit interpretation. Failure to reject is not proof of permanent stability.

questions.prompt: Why inspect a neighborhood of parameters rather than only the best setting?
questions.answer: A sharp isolated optimum can indicate noise fitting or hidden sensitivity; nearby results reveal how fragile the selected configuration is.
questions.explanation: Sensitivity is part of evidence quality, not another opportunity to optimize the final test.

reviewPrompts: Which change in the data would invalidate the model assumption?

lessons.title: Evaluate a modest ML signal without leakage
objectives: Build lagged features and train-only preprocessing.
Compare probability calibration and decision costs with a simple baseline.

topics.title: Model boundaries
details: Features, labels and predictions carry separate availability times.
A prediction score is not an executable order or assured return.

topics.title: Evaluation
details: Thresholds are chosen on validation data, not the final block.
Calibration, false positives and turnover matter alongside classification accuracy.

video.locator: 5.Py Cross-Validation I 2023: validation concepts; replace random folds with the interval-aware chronological splitter already built.

reading.locator: TimeSeriesSplit examples and gap parameter; document separately how preprocessing, label horizons and threshold selection respect the same boundary.

assignment.title: A calibrated synthetic-signal comparison
instructions: Fit a small logistic model or a simple probability table to lagged synthetic features using train-only transforms.
Compare a constant-probability baseline and choose any action threshold only on development folds.
Evaluate calibration, false positives, turnover and net paper results on the frozen block; retain a future-feature contamination test.
acceptanceCriteria: No forward return appears among the available features.
Threshold selection is separated from the final report.
Higher accuracy alone is not presented as evidence of a profitable executable strategy.

questions.prompt: A model has better direction accuracy but much higher turnover. What remains necessary?
choices: Selecting the model using direction accuracy alone
Annualizing accuracy to estimate expected net return
Cost-aware evaluation under the execution and risk model
questions.answer: Cost-aware evaluation under the execution and risk model
questions.explanation: Accuracy does not encode payoff size, timing, costs or capacity. Decisions must be evaluated through the full paper system.

questions.prompt: Why can fitting an imputer on all observations leak information even when the model sees only training rows?
questions.answer: The imputation parameters can reflect the distribution of later data, indirectly injecting future information into training features.
questions.explanation: The information boundary applies to every learned transformation, not just model.fit.

reviewPrompts: Which model improvement survives realistic decision costs?

lessons.title: Detect deliberately contaminated research results
objectives: Design checks for future joins, survivor-only universes and selective trials.
Produce a reviewable rejection or bounded acceptance decision.

topics.title: Adversarial validation
details: Plant known faults in isolated copies of the research pipeline.
Tests should fail on the intended fault without hiding other failures.

topics.title: Evidence standards
details: A clean result requires traceability through data, model and simulation.
Unresolved discrepancies must remain visible in the report.

reading.locator: General guidance and good practice for testing; Acceptance and Regression Testing, including Limitations of Regression Testing. Use negative controls as evidence of detection capability.

assignment.title: Advanced evidence gate: a leakage challenge pack
instructions: Create separate intentionally flawed copies with a future revision, a survivor-only universe, global preprocessing and omitted failed trials.
Run your checks against each flawed copy and the clean baseline, recording why each finding matters.
Add portfolio stress and cost sensitivity to an audit memo that may reject the candidate.
deliverables: Four contamination fixtures and failing checks
acceptanceCriteria: Every planted fault is detected by a named check.
The clean version remains reproducible with no unexplained ledger differences.
The memo states remaining limitations and does not infer profitability from passing tests.

questions.prompt: Why include a deliberately leaky copy in the audit pack?
choices: To show that the check can actually detect the known fault
To tune the validation checks until the final metric becomes positive
To replace untouched evaluation with data containing known faults
questions.answer: To show that the check can actually detect the known fault
questions.explanation: A negative control makes the test's detection capability observable. It must be isolated and never passed off as valid research.

questions.prompt: Does detecting all planted faults prove the research is free of leakage?
questions.answer: No. It establishes coverage of those known fault classes; other data paths, assumptions and unknown errors still need review.
questions.explanation: An audit should bound its claim and identify untested surfaces.

reviewPrompts: Which high-scoring result should the audit reject?

modules.title: 07. Paper execution, monitoring and safe recovery
modules.description: Build operational safeguards in an offline adapter that cannot send real orders.

lessons.title: Design a disconnected, idempotent paper adapter
objectives: Isolate order intent from execution transport.
Deduplicate retries and reconcile acknowledgements without a live endpoint.

topics.title: Execution boundary
details: The only adapter is an in-memory or local-file simulator.
No broker credentials, SDK, network order transport or live mode is included.

topics.title: Idempotency
details: A stable intent ID prevents retry from duplicating exposure.
Acknowledgement is not the same as a complete fill.

reading.locator: Chapter 4 Our First Use Case: Flask API and Service Layer and Chapter 6 Unit of Work Pattern; separate orchestration and durable state from adapters.

assignment.title: A simulator-only execution interface
instructions: Define submit, cancel and reconcile interfaces implemented only by a local fake exchange.
Persist stable intent IDs and simulate lost acknowledgements, duplicate submissions and partial fills.
Run with network access disabled and show that no live transport or credentials are needed or accepted.
acceptanceCriteria: Retrying one intent cannot create a second position.
Duplicate IDs with conflicting payloads fail visibly.
The runnable system contains no broker integration, live mode or secret configuration.

questions.prompt: An acknowledgement is lost after a simulated order is accepted. What should a retry reuse?
choices: A new ID that may duplicate exposure
The previous fill ID even when it belongs to another order
The same stable intent ID
questions.answer: The same stable intent ID
questions.explanation: Stable identity lets the receiver distinguish a retry from a new economic intent and return the existing state.

questions.prompt: Why exclude a live-adapter switch rather than merely leave it disabled?
questions.answer: Removing the capability prevents accidental real orders and keeps the exercise's safety boundary verifiable.
questions.explanation: A missing dangerous capability is a stronger boundary than a default that can be misconfigured.

reviewPrompts: Can any path convert this exercise into a live trade?

lessons.title: Monitor freshness, drift and limit breaches
objectives: Distinguish data/system health alerts from uncertain strategy drift signals.
Persist a fail-closed halt with explicit restart authorization.

topics.title: Monitoring contracts
details: Freshness, lag, queue length and reconciliation are operational signals.
Model drift is a diagnostic, not proof of a profitable replacement.

topics.title: Kill switches
details: A halt blocks new exposure even after a process restart.
Alert ownership and acknowledgement are part of the control.

reading.locator: Chapter 6 Monitoring Distributed Systems: actionable symptoms and avoiding noisy alerts; adapt to data freshness, reconciliation and simulated order health.

assignment.title: A durable no-new-exposure switch
instructions: Inject stale data, queue lag, a position mismatch and a paper loss-limit breach using deterministic clock control.
Persist the halt reason and reject new exposure while retaining current obligations.
Restart the process, verify the halt remains, then require an explicit reconciled clearance record with an owner.
acceptanceCriteria: All four injected conditions are visible and assigned a response.
Restart cannot bypass the halt.
A harmless transient and a true breach are distinguished using a documented threshold policy.

questions.prompt: Which signal most directly invalidates a paper position-risk calculation?
choices: A lower average return on a short but fully reconciled sample
An unresolved position reconciliation mismatch
A changed deployment label with identical verified code and input hashes
questions.answer: An unresolved position reconciliation mismatch
questions.explanation: If inventory is uncertain, exposure and admission checks cannot be trusted. New exposure should stop pending reconciliation.

questions.prompt: Why should a model-drift alert not automatically trigger a new optimized model?
questions.answer: Drift may reflect data faults or a changed regime; automatic optimization can introduce unvalidated behavior and selection bias.
questions.explanation: Investigate, evaluate and approve a versioned change instead of turning an alert into permission to retrain on the test.

reviewPrompts: What happens if the operator ignores an alert?

lessons.title: Recover from a checkpoint without duplicating effects
objectives: Define durable event and checkpoint boundaries.
Reconcile replayed state before resuming paper execution.

topics.title: Recovery model
details: A checkpoint must identify the last included event.
Replaying a suffix requires stable IDs and idempotent effects.

topics.title: Operations evidence
details: Backups need a tested restoration procedure.
Measure recovery on the exercise rather than inventing a service guarantee.

reading.locator: Runtime testing and Acceptance and Regression Testing: apply checks to a crash/restart contract, including limitations of regression coverage.

assignment.title: An interrupted-replay recovery drill
instructions: Checkpoint after a partial fill, then simulate a crash between event persistence and acknowledgement.
Restore, replay the suffix and compare with an uninterrupted golden run.
Corrupt a copied checkpoint and demonstrate a visible rejection and fallback to a verified earlier snapshot without deleting evidence.
deliverables: Interrupted/uninterrupted comparison and measured drill timings
acceptanceCriteria: Cash, positions, IDs and halt state match the uninterrupted run.
No fill or fee is applied twice.
Corrupt input fails visibly and recovery preserves an audit trail.

questions.prompt: Which checkpoint field is essential for safe suffix replay?
choices: The number of submitted orders without their fill identities
Only a wall-clock timestamp shared by several different events
The last included event identity/sequence
questions.answer: The last included event identity/sequence
questions.explanation: The replay boundary determines which effects are already represented. Without it, effects can be lost or applied twice.

questions.prompt: What must be reconciled before a recovered engine resumes?
questions.answer: Cash, positions, pending orders, event sequence, risk limits, data freshness and any persistent halt or unresolved exception.
questions.explanation: Loading a file is not proof that the operational state is safe to use.

reviewPrompts: Which crash boundary has the greatest duplicate-effect risk?

modules.title: 08. Reproducible paper-engine capstone and review
modules.description: Deliver an inspectable local system whose safety and research limitations are part of the result.

lessons.title: Package a versioned research and execution artifact
objectives: Bind data, code, parameters and reports to a manifest.
Reproduce the system without private data or paid services.

topics.title: Artifact lineage
details: Hashes identify exact fixtures and configurations.
A dependency lock and explicit run command reduce environment drift.

topics.title: Release discipline
details: Reports are outputs of the pinned run, not manually edited successes.
No credentials or restricted data enter the bundle.

reading.locator: Reproducible Environments and Version Control for Data: capture the environment and immutable inputs necessary to repeat a result.

assignment.title: A one-command paper artifact
instructions: Package original synthetic inputs, environment versions, code revision, split definitions, model parameters and expected output checksums.
Provide one command that validates, tests and regenerates all final tables locally.
Reproduce in a clean directory with no network; inventory licenses for any optional public data or dependency.
acceptanceCriteria: Changing a fixture causes a manifest mismatch or a new version, not silent replacement.
The bundle has no tokens, broker settings or private datasets.
A clean rerun regenerates the reported ledger and evaluation.

questions.prompt: Why record a data hash rather than only a file name?
choices: It confirms that the fixture represents future market regimes
It replaces historical membership and availability-time metadata
The name can stay the same while contents change
questions.answer: The name can stay the same while contents change
questions.explanation: A content hash binds the run to exact bytes. It establishes neither validity nor permission to reuse the data.

questions.prompt: Which artifacts are needed beyond model weights?
questions.answer: Feature definitions, preprocessing, availability and split policies, code/environment versions, cost/risk parameters and source data identity.
questions.explanation: Weights alone cannot reconstruct the decision system or its information boundary.

reviewPrompts: Can a reviewer regenerate tables without trusting your notebook state?

lessons.title: Deliver a reproducible and guarded paper engine
objectives: Integrate causal research, accounting and operational controls.
Demonstrate failure handling through executable evidence rather than architecture claims.

topics.title: End-to-end contract
details: Data quality, research selection and execution controls form one chain.
No positive-return target substitutes for correctness and safety.

topics.title: Acceptance evidence
details: Reviewers can replay a normal run and named failure drills.
Unresolved critical defects prevent a readiness claim.

reading.locator: Reality-model categories and liquid-market assumptions: audit which mechanisms your engine represents and which it explicitly omits.

assignment.title: Capstone: causal research to disconnected paper operations
instructions: Integrate your fixture/vintage pipeline, delayed baseline, event simulator, interval-aware evaluation, trial registry and constrained portfolio.
Add the simulator-only adapter, monitoring, persistent kill switch and crash/recovery workflow; expose no live transport.
Deliver the versioned bundle with a normal replay and stale-data, duplicate-event, partial-fill, leakage and recovery drills; a losing strategy is acceptable.
deliverables: Runnable local repository and immutable manifest
OOS/benchmark, cost, turnover, drawdown and stress report
Automated fault suite with actual outputs
Operations runbook, halt/restart transcript and limitation register
acceptanceCriteria: Decisions use only available vintages and historical membership.
Accounting, partial fills, costs and pending exposure reconcile.
Purged chronological evaluation and full trial history are inspectable.
The final test does not choose parameters or thresholds.
Halts persist and recovery matches uninterrupted replay without duplicate effects.
Execution is disconnected; there are no broker credentials, live mode or required paid services.
All reported outputs regenerate from the pinned command; no profitability guarantee or certification claim is made.

questions.prompt: Which finding should block capstone acceptance despite a positive backtest?
choices: The strategy loses under a disclosed stress scenario
The kill switch resets silently after a restart
The report includes rejected trials
questions.answer: The kill switch resets silently after a restart
questions.explanation: A broken operational safeguard invalidates the claimed control. Transparent losses and rejected trials are legitimate evidence, not defects to hide.

questions.prompt: Why does a passing capstone not justify live deployment?
questions.answer: Synthetic evidence and simplified models do not establish market validity, regulatory suitability, funding resilience or production execution safety.
questions.explanation: Professional Practice is a learning level. Live activity would require separate expertise, permissions and risk decisions outside this track.

reviewPrompts: Can the reviewer reproduce both the happy path and the stop path?

lessons.title: Run an independent challenge and close the research record
objectives: Respond to reviewer counterexamples without editing historical evidence.
Issue a bounded paper-only continue, revise or retire decision.

topics.title: Review protocol
details: A peer or delayed blind self-review selects tests, not the author alone.
Corrections produce new versions with comparable reports.

topics.title: Decision governance
details: Residual risk and open issues have owners and deadlines.
Retiring an unsupported idea is a valid professional learning outcome.

reading.locator: Guide for Ethical Research: Data Hazards; identify affected parties, misleading claims and remaining mitigations in your release record.

assignment.title: A challenge-response release memo
instructions: Give a reviewer the pinned bundle and ask them to reproduce a losing trade, a rejected order and a recovery boundary.
Record three challenges to data validity, execution realism or evaluation selection; rerun after any correction under a new version.
Publish a paper-only continue/revise/retire memo with unresolved limitations and a source-currency check.
deliverables: Version comparison and final decision memo
acceptanceCriteria: The reviewer-selected cases reconcile or remain openly unresolved.
Corrections preserve the prior evidence and trial count.
The conclusion is proportional to the tested claims and contains no live-trading or profitability authorization.

questions.prompt: What should happen when a reviewer finds an invalid availability timestamp?
choices: Keep the old final metric and call the timing error a sensitivity issue
Retune on the affected final block before reporting it as unchanged evidence
Correct it in a new version and rerun affected evidence
questions.answer: Correct it in a new version and rerun affected evidence
questions.explanation: A timing defect can invalidate all dependent results. Versioned correction and reevaluation preserve an honest record.

questions.prompt: What makes a retire decision useful evidence?
questions.answer: It states the rejected claim, reproducible reasons, known assumptions and what genuinely new evidence would be needed to reconsider.
questions.explanation: Stopping unsupported work is part of disciplined research, not a failure to manufacture an attractive outcome.

reviewPrompts: Which claim survived challenge, and which did you withdraw?

sources.title: pandas temporal data reference
sources.notes: Public HTML verified; explicit bar/session and publication policies remain the learner's responsibility.

sources.title: Chronological split and gap reference
sources.notes: Not an automatic solution to overlapping labels or point-in-time leakage.

sources.title: QuantConnect research concepts
sources.notes: Free documentation only; no hosted service, data subscription or account is required.

limitations: Algorithmic Trading is synthetic, historical and paper-only. Build a disconnected local simulator: no real money, broker connection, live mode, credential entry or guaranteed-profit claim.
Professional Practice is a learning level, not professional qualification, certification or authorization to deploy a financial service.

Use original synthetic fixtures for the required route. Public historical data are optional only with provenance, permitted use, historical membership and availability timestamps; do not scrape restricted feeds.

Reused Common Foundation, Quant, SDE and AI lessons retain their original IDs and progress. They provide prerequisite concepts; this track's applied assignments are distinct evidence, not duplicate credits.
The full route uses free local Python tooling and free official readings. Optional platform features, paid market data, cloud hosting and certificates are not required.
Backtests omit aspects of actual markets, operations and law. Deterministic replay, statistical metrics and passing tests do not establish trading profitability or suitability.
